configurePresets.name: linux-clang-asan
configurePresets.description: #213. The fuzz targets carry -fsanitize=fuzzer,address,undefined, so this is their natural lane, and tier1's matrix selects lanes purely by preset name with no per-lane -D overrides -- a workflow flag would be the special case here, not the preset. It also keeps local reproduction of the CI lane accurate. COSTS, measured rather than assumed: ~19 s wall / 57 s user at -j6 to build all 15 fuzz targets (a 4-vCPU runner is slower, and these are 15 fresh links competing for the same cores); the 6 corpus replays run in 0.32 s. No existing object's command line changes, so no compiler-cache entry is invalidated. DISK: the 15 binaries total 357 MB against this lane's documented ~18 G of instrumented executables (~2%) -- small, but stated because this is the disk-tightest leg in the matrix and it has died with `ld: final link failed: No space left on device` before; if that recurs this is one of the things to weigh. ASYMMETRY, deliberate: linux-clang-libc++-asan does NOT set FIXPP_BUILD_FUZZ. One lane replaying the corpora is the regression guard #213 asked for; a second would duplicate the cost without covering any additional seed.

testPresets.name: linux-clang-debug
testPresets.description: Debug. jobs=4 — #267 phase 2, MEASURED 2.10x by an A-B-A run on ONE VM (j=1 1142.1 s, j=4 541.5 s, j=1 1135.3 s — the two serial passes agree to 0.6%, so there is no pass-order effect), with a CPU calibration between passes flat and /proc/stat steal 0 throughout. ~597 s = 10 min/run. See ci/ctest-parallelism-probe.md.

testPresets.name: linux-clang-ubsan
testPresets.description: UBSan. jobs=4 — #267 phase 2, MEASURED 1.79x (1993 -> 1114 s, ~14.6 min/run) by a PAIRED same-VM run, cross-validated on a second VM to 1.9%/4.2%. Peak 0.65 -> 0.86 GiB, 5.5% of a 15.61 GiB runner. ⚠️ Do NOT copy to another lane without ITS OWN paired measurement: between-VM wall-clock variance is 27-43%, so only a paired same-VM run can decide a lane. debug was separately confirmed at 2.10x; tsan's j=2-vs-j=4 question is UNRESOLVED (its comparison was unpaired). See ci/ctest-parallelism-probe.md. || #268 — UBSAN_OPTIONS BELONGS HERE, NOT IN THE WORKFLOW. UBSan's default mode is RECOVERABLE: a finding prints 'runtime error:', execution continues, and the process exits 0 — so this lane ran the whole suite for its entire existence and could not go red on a UBSan finding, while /speckit-verify set halt_on_error=1 BY HAND at every gate. That asymmetry between CI and local IS the defect, so the fix is put where both read it: a testPresets environment reaches ctest and ctest passes it to every test, so CI, a developer's `ctest --preset`, and /speckit-verify all now get the same behaviour from one place — where a workflow `env:` would have fixed CI and left the asymmetry intact. Proven by a paired local A/B on one binary (2026-08-18, clang-22): the same signed-overflow test PASSES with ctest exiting 0 without this environment, and FAILS with it, print_stacktrace=1 yielding a real frame list. ⚠️ A preset environment value OVERRIDES the inherited one, so a hand-set UBSAN_OPTIONS no longer composes with it — add options here rather than around the invocation.

testPresets.name: linux-clang-tsan
testPresets.description: TSan. jobs=4 — #267 phase 1. ⚠️ ⚠️ CHANGED WITHOUT THE PAIRED A-B-A RUN THIS LANE'S OWN NOTE REQUIRED, ON AN EXPLICIT DECISION TO PROCEED. Recorded plainly so nobody later cites this value as measured: it is NOT. The prior text stands as the evidence standard and is reproduced here — the j=2-vs-j=4 comparison was made across TWO SEPARATE RUNS on a lane whose between-VM wall-clock spread is 43.3% (1903/2160/1376 s at an unchanged j=2), so it resolved nothing, and an earlier claim of 'no gain at j=4' was WITHDRAWN. What IS solid and unchanged: peak RSS reproduces to <2%, so j=4's +36% memory is real (2.53 GiB, ~16% of a 15.61 GiB runner — headroom, not a risk); and debug (2.10x, A-B-A) and ubsan (1.79x, paired) both gained when measured properly, which is the ANALOGY this change rests on rather than a measurement of THIS lane. ⚠️ THE OPEN RISK IS NOT MEMORY, IT IS SANITIZER BEHAVIOUR UNDER LOAD: per [const] and #267 acceptance item 5, any TSan warning that appears after this widening is a REAL DEFECT until disproven, never a 'parallelism artifact'. If this lane becomes flaky, revert to jobs=2 first and measure second. Settle it properly with the paired A-B-A design (serial, parallel, serial; the two serial passes must agree, as debug's did to 0.6%) before treating 4 as established. See ci/ctest-parallelism-probe.md.

testPresets.name: linux-clang-libc++-ubsan
testPresets.description: #268 — the Tier 3 twin, and it is NOT optional. This lane reproduces the same recoverable-mode gap and the same finding as linux-clang-ubsan: run 32024674144 job 95371515603 recorded 1 report, ran 356/356, ctest green. Fixing one ubsan lane and not the other is the enumeration trap ci/expected-sanitizer-reports.txt's header already paid for once, when an allowlist named linux-clang-asan and missed linux-clang-libc++-asan. See linux-clang-ubsan's description for the full rationale.
